provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Athletics: long jump
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state the rules of long jump
The pupils should be able to demonstrate a proper long jump technique
Introduction:
Today we will learn about long jump which is a popular event in sports day. We have all seen how athletes jump far in competitions.
Content:
Long jump is an athletic event where you run and jump as far as possible into a sand pit. To do a long jump you need to run fast on the track then jump off one foot. Stretch your body forward while in the air. Land with both feet together in the sand pit. Your jump is measured from the take-off board to the nearest mark in the sand. Like when we measure our classroom in metres.
Class activity:
We will practice long jump in the school field. Pupils will take turns running and jumping into the sand pit. We will measure each jump with a tape measure.
Evaluation questions:
What is the first step in long jump?
How should you land after jumping?
What do we use to measure the jump?
Summary:
Long jump is fun and helps us build strong legs and body coordination.

topics.title: Ball games: handball
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain how to pass a handball
The pupils should be able to demonstrate proper shooting technique
Introduction:
We have played with balls before like football. Today we will learn handball which uses our hands instead of feet.
Content:
Handball is a game where you throw a ball into a goal. You can run with the ball but you must bounce it or take three steps then pass. To pass the ball, hold it with two hands and push it towards your teammate. For shooting, aim at the goal and throw the ball with force. Like throwing a stone into a river but more controlled. The team with the most goals wins.
Class activity:
We will divide into two teams and play a mini handball match. Pupils will practice passing and shooting during the game.
Evaluation questions:
How many steps can you take with the ball?
What is the main goal in handball?
Name one rule of handball.
Summary:
Handball teaches us teamwork and how to use our hands for ball control.

topics.title: Fitness circuits
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list three fitness exercises
The pupils should be able to demonstrate proper form for each exercise
Introduction:
We all know that exercise makes us strong and healthy. Today we will do different exercises at different stations in our fitness circuit.
Content:
A fitness circuit has many exercise stations. At each station you do a different exercise for one minute. Common stations include jumping jacks, running in place, push-ups and sit-ups. Like when we do morning assembly but with more movement. After one minute, you move to the next station. You rest for 30 seconds between stations. We will keep track of how many exercises we complete.
Class activity:
We will set up five exercise stations around the field. Pupils will rotate through each station, doing the exercise for one minute.
Evaluation questions:
How long do you exercise at each station?
What is rest time between stations?
Name one exercise you might do in a fitness circuit.
Summary:
Fitness circuits help us build strength and stamina through varied exercises.

topics.title: Nutrition and exercise
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify foods that give us energy
The pupils should be able to create a simple exercise plan
Introduction:
We have learned about different food groups. Today we will see how food and exercise work together to keep us healthy.
Content:
Good food gives us energy for exercise. Carbohydrates like rice and yam give quick energy. Proteins like beans and fish help build muscles. We need to eat before and after exercise. Before exercise eat light food like banana. After exercise eat protein to help muscles grow. Exercise helps our body use food better. Like a car needs petrol to move, our body needs food to exercise.
Class activity:
Pupils will create a one-week exercise plan showing what to eat before and after each activity.
Evaluation questions:
Which food gives quick energy?
When should we eat protein?
Why do we need food for exercise?
Summary:
Good nutrition and proper exercise help us grow strong and stay healthy.

topics.title: Community health
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain why clean environment is important
The pupils should be able to participate in communal labour activities
Introduction:
We all live in communities like our school and compound. Keeping these places clean helps prevent diseases.
Content:
A clean environment prevents sickness from germs. We should throw rubbish in bins not on the ground. Our school has a bin day where we clean the compound. Communal labour is when we work together to clean public places. Like when we clean our classroom together. Clean water and good toilets are also important for community health.
Class activity:
We will participate in a communal labour activity by cleaning the school compound and arranging the dustbins properly.
Evaluation questions:
Why is a clean environment important?
What is communal labour?
Name one way to keep our community healthy.
Summary:
Keeping our environment clean helps prevent diseases and keeps everyone healthy.

topics.title: Safety on the road
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate proper road crossing
The pupils should be able to identify a zebra crossing
Introduction:
Many of us walk to school and cross busy roads. Today we will learn how to stay safe when crossing roads.
Content:
Road safety rules help prevent accidents. Always look left and right before crossing. Use zebra crossings which are white stripes on the road. Like the one near our school gate. Wait for the green light at pedestrian crossings. Do not run across the road. Walk in a straight line and not between parked cars. Always hold an adult's hand when crossing busy roads.
Class activity:
We will practice road crossing in the school yard using chalk to draw a zebra crossing.
Evaluation questions:
What should you do before crossing a road?
What is a zebra crossing?
Why should you not run across the road?
Summary:
Following road safety rules helps prevent accidents and keeps us safe.

topics.title: Martial play
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate basic wrestling holds
The pupils should be able to explain the importance of rules in martial play
Introduction:
We have seen wrestling on TV during sports programs. Today we will learn safe wrestling basics that we can practice in class.
Content:
Martial play is safe wrestling with rules. We learn to control our bodies and respect others. Basic holds include the shoulder lock and leg grab. Like when we play amodu game but with more structure. The most important rule is safety-no hitting or hurting. We must always listen to the teacher and stop when asked. Martial play builds strength and discipline.
Class activity:
We will practice basic wrestling holds with partners on mats, following all safety rules.
Evaluation questions:
What is the most important rule in martial play?
Name one basic wrestling hold.
Why do we need rules in martial play?
Summary:
Martial play teaches us discipline and body control while keeping us safe.

topics.title: Rhythmic activities
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to march to a steady beat
The pupils should be able to create a simple rhythmic pattern
Introduction:
We all like music and moving to beats. Today we will learn how to march and move in rhythm together.
Content:
Rhythmic activities involve moving to beats and music. Marching is walking in time with a drum or clapping. We can march forward, backward or sideways. Like soldiers in a parade. We can also move our arms and legs to create patterns. Rhythmic activities help our coordination and memory. We will practice for our end of term display.
Class activity:
We will form lines and practice marching to drum beats, changing directions and arm movements.
Evaluation questions:
What is rhythmic movement?
How does marching help our body?
Why do we practice for displays?
Summary:
Rhythmic activities help us move together in time and improve our coordination.

topics.title: First aid and rescue
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate how to call for help
The pupils should be able to explain basic rescue shouts
Introduction:
Sometimes accidents happen and people need help. Today we will learn how to call for help in emergencies.
Content:
In an emergency, we need to call for help quickly. We can shout "Fire! Fire!" or "Help! Help!" to get attention. Like when we see someone in trouble at the river. We can also run to get an adult or use a phone if available. For rescue shouts, we can say "Hold on! Help is coming!" to calm someone in danger. Always stay calm when calling for help.
Class activity:
Pupils will practice different rescue shouts in pairs, pretending they are in different emergency situations.
Evaluation questions:
What should you shout in a fire emergency?
How can we get attention in an emergency?
Why is it important to stay calm when calling for help?
Summary:
Knowing how to call for help can save lives in emergency situations.

topics.title: Revision and sports festival
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to participate in inter-house sports
The pupils should be able to demonstrate skills learned this term
Introduction:
This week we will revise what we learned and have our sports festival. We will show our parents and teachers what we can do.
Content:
In our sports festival, we will have inter-house mini sports. Each house will compete in different events like long jump, handball and relay races. We will also display our rhythmic activities and martial play skills. Like during cultural day but with sports. The winning house will get certificates. Everyone who participates will get a certificate for trying their best.
Class activity:
We will have inter-house competitions in long jump, handball and relay races, followed by a display of rhythmic activities.
Evaluation questions:
What is inter-house sports?
What will you get for participating?
Name one event in our sports festival.
Summary:
The sports festival celebrates our learning and gives us a chance to show our skills.
